A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ZeroBench and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Corresponding methods, evaluations and failure examples can be matched, while dataset revisions and new experiments are identifiable.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 20 LMMs, including main-question and subquestion scores, completion-token measurements and qualitative failure analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports revised baseline results, additional model evaluations, a human study, quantitative error analysis, formatting evaluations and visual-hint experiments.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction process gains post-release community red teaming and further adversarial refinement (Section 3.2). Human question creation, adversarial filtering and subquestion decomposition remain the core procedure. Changing the initial pipeline from four steps to three merely combines feedback and initial evaluation.

E1.justification: The benchmark retains 100 main questions and 334 subquestions, but dataset v2 modifies 23% of main questions, including corrections to incorrect or ambiguous answers (Section 3.2; Appendix A.2). v3 also introduces a bounded test scenario supplying visual hints on 37 questions. The overall visual-question-answering coverage remains similar.

E2.justification: The original 20-model roster is retained, while Table 7 adds 26 post-release model/configuration entries, including Gemini 3 Pro, GPT-5.2 and Llama 4 variants. Section 5.2 adds a human comparator, and Table 3 additionally evaluates GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.1 Pro in the error comparison.

E3.justification: v3 adds a post-release protocol reporting only pass@5 and pass∧5, a human evaluation using ten question subsets with five independently duplicated subsets, and a 37-question experiment varying hints from zero to three. Error-category discovery and assignment use different response samplings. These substantially expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v1 primarily provides qualitative failure examples. v3 adds quantitative classification into nine error categories, question-level correctness analysis, formatting/refusal analysis across models, and an intervention testing whether visual hints reduce failures (Figures 8, 10–12; Tables 3 and 8). The earlier appendix failure cases are largely retained.

E5.justification: v3 adds human-score standard deviations and correlation across duplicated question sets, plus 95% confidence intervals for formatting accuracy (Figure 12). The existing CLT standard errors for subquestions and five-sample model evaluations remain; the PDFs do not establish an increased repetition count for those retained evaluations.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes results following dataset revision: Gemini 2 Flash Thinking's pass@5 changes from 7% to 5%, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2's subquestion score from 24.30% to 25.50%. New results include Gemini 3 Pro's 19% pass@5, GPT-5.2's 6% pass∧5, human performance of 29.5% and quantified hint benefits. Revised-dataset scores are not same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: The accuracy, averaged subquestion accuracy and CLT standard-error definitions are retained. Renaming k/k reliability to pass∧k preserves the all-samples-correct criterion. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3 adds no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: v1 centres its contribution on a benchmark impossible for contemporary models. v3 explicitly restricts impossibility to original release and adds a central claim of sustained difficulty over a year, supported by tracking 46 baselines and reporting remaining headroom. Human comparison also becomes a headline contribution.

C2.justification: v1 speculates about future saturation and higher-resolution inputs. v3 interprets observed progress, overlapping solved questions and hint benefits, while cautioning that outputs cannot identify the architectural causes of improvements (Appendix D.3). Appendix F adds substantive limitations concerning sampling variance, manual curation, overfitting and alignment with deployed tasks.

D1.justification: Appendices A, B.5 and D add curator/evaluator details, dataset-v2 API access dates and Nebius usage, and complete prompts and rules for error discovery, consolidation and assignment. Earlier inference prompts, hardware and hyperparameters are largely retained or relocated. Exact settings for the expanded post-release evaluations remain less fully documented.

R1.justification: The difficult-visual-benchmark positioning remains. v3 adds a small-scale evaluations subsection citing FrontierScience, GDPval and FrontierCS, cites τ-bench for reliability, and introduces longitudinal comparisons with ARC-AGI-2 and HLE. Medical-benchmark and Visual Riddles discussions are removed, alongside additions of newer model references.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative around pre-release and post-release evaluation, rewrites the abstract and conclusion, consolidates experimental setup, and moves inference and completion-token material into the appendix. The appendix is reorganized into construction, protocols, additional results, error analysis, failure cases and limitations.

P2.justification: v3 adds longitudinal, correctness-grid, hint and formatting plots, together with human, post-release and error-analysis tables. Figure 3 replaces two illustrative examples; Table 2 changes from full-width to a compact single-column display; the completion-token table moves to the appendix. Retained failure-case figures are also reformatted.

improvement.justification: Community red teaming corrects incorrect or non-unique answers, addressing an important benchmark-validity weakness acknowledged in v3 (Section 3.2; Appendix A.2). Human evaluation, longitudinal tracking, quantified errors and hint interventions substantially strengthen evidence beyond v1's initial scores and qualitative examples. Post-release settings and human test timing remain incompletely documented, but the corrections and stronger validation establish a substantial net improvement.
